contract: Road user a overtakes and passes road user b on b's right: a overtakes and passes b from the rear, as drv.interaction.overtake_pass states it with the same window and the same heading tolerance, and makes the passage with b on its left. b is on a's left where the lateral component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing) is positive; the two are side by side where their projections on a's heading share length (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero). The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos. The act is recognized at the observation at which drv.interaction.overtake_pass holds for a and b, where b is on a's left there and at every observation since the act began at which the two are side by side. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until b has again been ahead of a and then comes to be behind it. Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized. It denotes the relative motion of the two road users and the side on which a passes only: it says nothing of the lanes or the pavement a uses, of whether b moves, or of why a passes. Not denoted: a pass with b on a's right at the recognition or at some observation at which the two are side by side, which is a pass on b's left; a drawing alongside b that does not clear b; b ahead of a only while their headings are not aligned. Where b's bearing or the overlap of the two bodies is unobserved at an observation the passage reads, it is unknown.

params.name: window
params.meaning: the longest duration of the pass, from having b ahead to having it behind; conduct before the window is not read

params.name: same_dir_cos
params.meaning: cosine of the largest heading difference at which a and b count as travelling in the same direction

act.onset: The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos.
act.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which drv.interaction.overtake_pass holds for a and b, where b is on a's left there and at every observation since the act began at which the two are side by side.
act.extent: The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until b has again been ahead of a and then comes to be behind it.
act.history: Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized.

elements.span: a overtakes and passes b from the rear, as drv.interaction.overtake_pass states it with the same window and the same heading tolerance
elements.justification: The pass from the rear, its beginning, its recognition and its extent are those of drv.interaction.overtake_pass, whose contract denotes 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; this concept adds only the side, so it calls that concept with its own window and same_dir_cos rather than rebuilding it.

elements.span: b is on a's left where the lateral component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing) is positive
elements.justification: rel.bearing is the 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for "on the right of", "immediately to the rear")': its lateral component tells on which side of a the other road user lies, which is the side of the passage.

elements.span: the two are side by side where their projections on a's heading share length (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero)
elements.justification: rel.longitudinal_overlap: 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side): the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share'; its exclusion (neither a contact nor a distance between the bodies) does not apply, since only the side-by-side phase of the pass is read with it.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: a follows b in the same lane with headings aligned (rel.same_direction), b ahead with no longitudinal overlap; a moves to the right, draws alongside with b's bearing lateral component positive (b on a's left) while rel.longitudinal_overlap is non-negative, and comes to have b behind it with b still on its left, all within the window: the concept holds at the observation at which b first is behind a.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The same pass made with a moving to the left: while side by side, b's bearing lateral component is negative (b on a's right), and at recognition b is behind a on its right: drv.interaction.overtake_pass holds but the passage is on b's left, so the concept does not hold.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The pass of the holds scenario with rel.bearing not observed on the source: neither the order nor the side can be read.

contract: Road user a, moving, points to the left of the designated direction of travel of carrier region r by more than a tolerance: its heading has turned off r's direction toward the left. With h a's heading (kin.heading) and d r's designated direction (st.lane_direction), both as a formula reads them normalised, the dot product of d and h is positive, so that a points along d rather than against it, and the cross product d_x times h_y minus d_y times h_x exceeds sin_tol, so that h lies to the left of d, counter-clockwise in the world frame, by more than the angle whose sine is sin_tol; and a's speed (kin.speed) is above speed_tol. It is a state at one observation: it says nothing of whether a occupies r, of how long its heading has been so, of the path a will follow, or of why it turns. Not denoted: a road user at rest or moving at or below speed_tol; a heading within that angle of d, or turned to its right; a heading that points against d, the dot product being at or below zero. Where r carries no designated direction, or a's heading or speed is unobserved, it is unknown.

params.name: sin_tol
params.meaning: sine of the largest angle between a's heading and r's designated direction at which a counts as keeping to that direction: the heading noise and wander the observer tolerates

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed at or below which a counts as not moving: the source's speed resolution

elements.justification: kin.heading is the 'direction the body points', read normalised; the departure is of the body's pointing from the carrier's direction, not of a path.

st.lane_direction is the 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in', local to its carrier and unknown where none is carried, which is the reference the heading departs from.
kin.speed is the 'magnitude of velocity'; a road user at rest changes no course, so the state is read only while a moves above the tolerance.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: a moves well above speed_tol in lane r whose designated direction points east; a's heading points east-north-east, turned counter-clockwise from r's direction by clearly more than the angle whose sine is sin_tol: the concept holds.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: a moves in r with its heading aligned with r's designated direction (cross product below sin_tol): the concept does not hold.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: a moves turned to the left of the lane, but the source does not observe st.lane_direction for r.

contract: Road user a, moving, points to the right of the designated direction of travel of carrier region r by more than a tolerance: its heading has turned off r's direction toward the right. With h a's heading (kin.heading) and d r's designated direction (st.lane_direction), both as a formula reads them normalised, the dot product of d and h is positive, so that a points along d rather than against it, and the cross product d_x times h_y minus d_y times h_x is below minus sin_tol, so that h lies to the right of d, clockwise in the world frame, by more than the angle whose sine is sin_tol; and a's speed (kin.speed) is above speed_tol. It is a state at one observation: it says nothing of whether a occupies r, of how long its heading has been so, of the path a will follow, or of why it turns. Not denoted: a road user at rest or moving at or below speed_tol; a heading within that angle of d, or turned to its left; a heading that points against d, the dot product being at or below zero. Where r carries no designated direction, or a's heading or speed is unobserved, it is unknown.

params.name: sin_tol
params.meaning: sine of the largest angle between a's heading and r's designated direction at which a counts as keeping to that direction: the heading noise and wander the observer tolerates

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed at or below which a counts as not moving: the source's speed resolution

elements.justification: kin.heading is the 'direction the body points', read normalised; the departure is of the body's pointing from the carrier's direction, not of a path.

st.lane_direction is the 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in', local to its carrier and unknown where none is carried, which is the reference the heading departs from.
kin.speed is the 'magnitude of velocity'; a road user at rest changes no course, so the state is read only while a moves above the tolerance.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: a moves well above speed_tol in lane r whose designated direction points east; a's heading points east-south-east, turned clockwise from r's direction by clearly more than the angle whose sine is sin_tol: the concept holds.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: a moves in r with its heading aligned with r's designated direction (cross product above minus sin_tol): the concept does not hold.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: a moves turned to the right of the lane, but the source does not observe st.lane_direction for r.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
may overtake and pass upon the right of another vehicle only under the following conditions:
(a) When the driver of the vehicle overtaken is making or signaling to make a left turn.
(b) Upon a highway with unobstructed pavement which is not occupied by parked vehicles and which is of sufficient width for two or more lines of moving vehicles in each direction.
(c) Upon a highway with unobstructed pavement which is not marked as a traffic lane and which is not occupied by parked vehicles,
if the vehicle that is overtaking and passing another vehicle:
(1) Except as otherwise provided in subsection 4 [(4) appended below],
does not travel more than 200 feet in the section of pavement not marked as a traffic lane;
or (2) While being driven in the section of pavement not marked as a traffic lane, does not travel through an intersection
or past any private way that is used to enter or exit the highway.
(d) Upon any highway on which traffic is restricted to one direction of movement, where the highway is free from obstructions and of sufficient width for two or more lines of moving vehicles.
The provisions of subparagraph (1) of paragraph (c) of subsection 1 do not apply to: (a) An authorized emergency vehicle
described in NRS 484A.480;
(b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle
pursuant to NRS 484A.490;
(c) A traffic incident management vehicle;
(d) A tow car;
(e) A coroner vehicle;
or (f) A public transit motor bus,
that is being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway
where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder in that manner.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'), claimed whole, never expanded into classes. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080, 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role, not membership: it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency).

'overtake and pass upon the right of another vehicle' is the act drv.interaction.overtake_pass_on_right(subject, b), whose contract denotes 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b on b's right'; the other vehicle b is of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'only under the following conditions' forbids the act unless one of the listed conditions holds, so each condition is an exception to the prohibition.

The vehicle overtaken is b. 'signaling to make a left turn' is the signal itself, not a declared intention: sig.turn_indicator 'the turn indicator state in {off, left, right}' at left, or sig.hand_signal 'a driver's or rider's arm signal' of meaning left; the indicator's exclusion (not the turn itself) does not apply, since the words name the signal. 'is making ... a left turn' is b's act drv.motion.left_turn, 'Road user a has completed a turn to the left', read as recognized within its window ahead of the observation, so that a turn under way is caught by its completion (narrowing). 'the driver of' is read through b's controlled motion (agency).

'Upon a highway': the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) an st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'. 'unobstructed pavement': no st.obstruction ('a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user') lies on that way (st.on_way). 'not occupied by parked vehicles': no road user of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that is drv.motion.parked ('the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not') occupies a roadway (st.roadway) the subject occupies. 'sufficient width for two or more lines of moving vehicles in each direction': an st.lane is 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles', so width for two lines in a direction is a count of lanes in that direction (st.lane_adjacency 'the count of lanes in that direction') of at least the stated two, for every lane lying on the highway (each direction).

'pavement which is not marked as a traffic lane': the subject occupies an st.shoulder whose paved attribute is set ('the part of the highway beside the roadway ...; paved attribute'), or occupies an st.roadway while occupying no st.lane; 'unobstructed' and 'not occupied by parked vehicles' as in s4, read on the highway (st.on_way) and on the shoulder or roadway section the subject occupies (rel.occupies).

'does not travel more than 200 feet in the section of pavement not marked as a traffic lane': the distance the subject has travelled (kin.path_length, 'distance travelled along the body's path') while continuously occupying that section (a paved st.shoulder, or an st.roadway outside every st.lane), read with Term.distanceWhile at the recognition of the pass, is at most the stated 200 feet.

'While being driven in the section of pavement not marked as a traffic lane, does not travel through an intersection': since the subject came onto that section and while it stays on it, its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) no st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'; an alley junction is no st.intersection by that contract, as DEF-NRS-484A-105 (3) excludes it. 'being driven' is read through controlled motion (agency).

Nearest atoms only: 'past any private way that is used to enter or exit the highway' would be read as the subject's footprint overlapping the entrance of a private way while on the section. st.driveway_or_alley_entrance is 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway' and its contract states 'Not a stand-in for: which of them meets the highway there — the kind does not tell an alley's entrance from a private road's or driveway's'; a private way (DEF-NRS-484A-190, 'every way or place in private ownership') excludes an alley, which is a highway. The span is a gap.

'any highway on which traffic is restricted to one direction of movement': the subject occupies an st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction' — the restriction binds the road users of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, the aggregate the contract's 'traffic' carries. 'free from obstructions': no st.obstruction lies on the highway (st.on_way). 'sufficient width for two or more lines of moving vehicles': every lane on that highway has a lane count in its direction (st.lane_adjacency) of at least the stated two.

'do not apply to ... An authorized emergency vehicle': the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws'), never expanded; for its members the 200-foot limit of (c)(1) is met.

'A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle': such a vehicle is, by the words of DEF-NRS-484A-020, 'a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law', a member of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle, which the run's reading classifies; the span claims that aggregate whole.

'A traffic incident management vehicle': ru.official_vehicle 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service' of kind incident_management; its exclusion (not an emergency vehicle) agrees with the words.
'A tow car' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-280::tow_car, claimed whole.
'A coroner vehicle': ru.official_vehicle of kind coroner.

'bus' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus; the law's own qualifier 'public transit' limits its members to ru.transit_bus, 'bus in public transit service, identifiable by its livery or route display', leaving out school, private and charter buses.

'being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway': the exempt vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) an st.shoulder whose paved attribute is set, lying on the highway (st.on_way); 'being driven' is read through controlled motion (agency).

'lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder': a dev.regulatory_sign of code shoulder_use_permitted that governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — ... or shoulder') the shoulder occupied, whose conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold: 'any occupancy or class condition is met'); 'lawfully placed' is read through the sign's presence (observable_reading, status); the sign is not a stand-in for a manoeuvre, being read as a condition.

residues.why: The words point to subsection 4, whose exemption is carried by spans s12 to s21; they add no restriction of their own: the duty is the same whether or not they are read.
NRS 484A.480 is not a law of this corpus; the class it describes is carried by the aggregate on s12.
NRS 484A.490 is not a law of this corpus; the permitted class is carried by the aggregate on s14.

applicability: The subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, overtakes and passes on its right another road user b of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: drv.interaction.overtake_pass_on_right(subject, b) with p.overtake_window and p.overtake_same_direction_cos is recognized at the judged observation. b is quantified there, not a binder.
obligation: At that recognition at least one of the following holds; otherwise the duty is violated. (a) At every observation of the act, b shows sig.turn_indicator left or sig.hand_signal left, or drv.motion.left_turn(b) with p.turn_window, p.turn_heading_min, p.u_turn_heading_min and p.turn_yaw_rate_tol holds within p.turn_window ahead of that observation. (b) At every observation of the act, the subject occupies a highway h on which no st.obstruction lies (st.on_way), no road user of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that is drv.motion.parked (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.parking_min_duration) occupies a roadway the subject occupies, and every lane lying on h has, in its direction, an st.lane_adjacency count of at least the stated two. (c) At every observation of the act, the subject occupies a highway h on which no obstruction lies, and occupies pavement not marked as a lane (a paved st.shoulder, or an st.roadway while occupying no st.lane) that no parked vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle occupies; and, at recognition, either (c1) the path length travelled while continuously on that pavement (Term.distanceWhile) is at most the stated 200 feet, or the subject is exempt under subsection 4, or (c2) since it came onto that pavement it has occupied no st.intersection and no private-way entrance (the gap of span s10). Exempt under subsection 4: the subject is of DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle, of DEF-NRS-484A-280::tow_car, an ru.official_vehicle of kind incident_management or coroner, or of DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus and ru.transit_bus, and at every observation of the act it occupies a paved st.shoulder lying on the highway that a dev.regulatory_sign of code shoulder_use_permitted governs (dev.governs) with prim.conditions_hold for the subject. (d) At every observation of the act, the subject occupies an st.one_way_roadway on a highway on which no obstruction lies and every lane lying on that highway has an st.lane_adjacency count in its direction of at least the stated two.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.
'lawfully placed signage' is read through the presence of the shoulder-use sign governing the shoulder.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a two-way highway whose every lane has an st.lane_adjacency count of one in its direction, the subject follows b in the same lane, moves right within the roadway and lanes, and passes b with b on its left; b shows sig.turn_indicator off and sig.hand_signal no_signal and makes no left turn; the subject never occupies a shoulder: no condition holds.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: b is halted with sig.turn_indicator left at every observation of the act; the subject passes it on its right within the roadway: condition (a) holds.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject travels alone on the highway, no road user ahead of it; no pass is recognized.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject draws past b as in forbid but the source does not observe rel.bearing: whether a pass on the right occurred is unknown.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but b shows sig.turn_indicator left only during the first part of the act and off afterwards, and makes no left turn: (a) holds for part of the act only.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3_outside
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but b shows sig.turn_indicator left at every observation of the act, having shown off before the act began.

scenarios.name: occasion_s4
scenarios.narrative: The pass begins on a highway whose lanes count two in each direction and ends after a lane drop to one lane in each direction; b gives no signal: (b) holds for part of the act only.

scenarios.name: occasion_s4_outside
scenarios.narrative: The highway widens to two lanes in each direction before the act begins and keeps them through the act; no obstruction lies on it and no parked vehicle occupies the roadway: (b) holds throughout the act though not before it.

scenarios.name: occasion_s5
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes b partly on a paved shoulder and partly in a lane of a highway with one lane in each direction; b gives no signal: (c) holds for part of the act only.

scenarios.name: occasion_s5_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject moves onto a paved shoulder as the act begins, passes b on the shoulder over a short distance well below the stated limit, traversing no intersection and no driveway or alley entrance; no obstruction or parked vehicle there: (c) holds throughout the act.

scenarios.name: occasion_s11
scenarios.narrative: The pass begins on an st.one_way_roadway with two lanes in its direction and ends on a two-way highway with one lane in each direction; b gives no signal: (d) holds for part of the act only.

scenarios.name: occasion_s11_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject enters an st.one_way_roadway with two lanes as the act begins and passes b on its right there: (d) holds throughout the act.

scenarios.name: occasion_s20
scenarios.narrative: A ru.transit_bus subject passes b on a paved shoulder governed by a shoulder_use_permitted sign whose conditions hold, travelling far beyond the stated limit and through an intersection, but the bus occupies the shoulder for part of the act only, finishing in a lane: the exemption does not cover the act and (c) fails.

scenarios.name: occasion_s20_outside
scenarios.narrative: The same ru.transit_bus occupies the governed paved shoulder at every observation of the act, travelling far beyond the stated limit with no intersection or entrance on its path: exempt from (c)(1), (c) holds.

scenarios.name: occasion_s21
scenarios.narrative: A tow car of DEF-NRS-484A-280::tow_car passes b on a paved shoulder beyond the stated limit and through an intersection; a shoulder_use_permitted sign governs the shoulder for the first part of the act only, the shoulder further on being ungoverned.

scenarios.name: occasion_s21_outside
scenarios.narrative: The same tow car passes on a paved shoulder that the shoulder_use_permitted sign governs throughout the act, the sign's conditions holding, with no intersection or entrance on its path.

under_way.words: overtake and pass upon the right of another vehicle
under_way.justification: An observation inside the act lies after its beginning, the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, rel.same_direction), and at or before its recognition, while the subject's velocity (kin.velocity), exceeding b's along its heading, carries it up to and past b; before it b is still ahead and clear. These relations are computed from the two road users' kinematics, so the boundary reads their relative motion, never a place.

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of an overtaking manoeuvre on an urban street, from having the overtaken vehicle ahead to having it behind
param_proposals.source: overtaking-manoeuvre durations in naturalistic driving studies

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as travelling in the same direction while one moves out to pass the other
param_proposals.source: lane-change heading angles in naturalistic driving data

param_proposals.name: p.turn_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of a turn at a junction by a bicycle or a scooter, from the start of its heading change to its end
param_proposals.source: junction turning-time observations

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: intersection turning-geometry conventions

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: intersection turning-geometry conventions

param_proposals.name: p.turn_yaw_rate_tol
param_proposals.convention: the yaw-rate magnitude at or below which a road user's heading counts as no longer turning: the yaw-rate noise floor of the source
param_proposals.source: yaw-rate noise of the acquisition source

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition source

param_proposals.name: p.parking_min_duration
param_proposals.convention: the longest halt counted as temporary, as for loading or unloading: a common time limit of a passenger loading zone
param_proposals.source: municipal passenger-loading-zone time limits

gaps.proposal: `st.private_way_entrance` | the place where a way in private ownership — a private road or driveway — meets the highway, through which a vehicle enters or leaves the highway; the junction of an alley, a public way, with another way is not one **Not a stand-in for:** an alley's junction or an intersection | general
gaps.nearest: st.driveway_or_alley_entrance — 'Not a stand-in for: which of them meets the highway there — the kind does not tell an alley's entrance from a private road's or driveway's'; st.alley — a way within a block, not the place where a private way meets the highway

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
may overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right only
under conditions permitting such movement in safety.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'), claimed whole. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency).

'overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right' is the act drv.interaction.overtake_pass_on_right(subject, b), 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b on b's right'; b is of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'only' makes the act lawful only under the conditions of s3.

operationalizations.standard: under conditions permitting such movement in safety
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the movement is made in safety where, at every observation of the act, the subject is in contact (rel.contact) with no road user and no road user's closest approach to it under constant velocities (prim.closest_approach_within over p.conflict_horizon) comes closer than p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); the closest-approach distance is the measured magnitude the bound is compared with, so the verdict moves with how close the conflict is.

applicability: The subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, overtakes and passes on its right another road user b of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: drv.interaction.overtake_pass_on_right(subject, b) with p.overtake_window and p.overtake_same_direction_cos is recognized at the judged observation; b is quantified there, not a binder.
obligation: At every observation of the act, from its beginning (the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with aligned headings) to its recognition, for every road user u other than the subject (b included): the subject is not in rel.contact with u, and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Otherwise the duty is violated. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence on the safety standard, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.

The catch-all 'conditions permitting such movement in safety' is read only through conflicts with road users: contact and closest approaches under constant velocities. Conditions of the road (surface, view) enter only through those conflicts.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes b on b's right and, while side by side, closes laterally on b so that their closest approach within p.conflict_horizon falls below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes b on b's right in the adjacent lane keeping its distance; no closest approach within p.conflict_horizon falls below p.conflict_centre_clearance and no contact occurs; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject follows b in the same lane at a steady gap and never passes it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject draws past b on its right but rel.bearing is not observed: whether a pass on the right occurred is unknown.

under_way.words: overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right
under_way.justification: An observation inside the act lies after its beginning, the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, rel.same_direction), and at or before its recognition, while the subject's velocity (kin.velocity), exceeding b's along its heading, carries it up to and past b. These relations are computed from the two road users' kinematics, so the boundary reads their relative motion, never a place.

param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of an overtaking manoeuvre on an urban street, from having the overtaken vehicle ahead to having it behind
param_proposals.source: overtaking-manoeuvre durations in naturalistic driving studies

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cos

param_proposals.source: lane-change heading angles in naturalistic driving data

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique; FHWA Surrogate Safety Assessment Model

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO passenger-car design-vehicle dimensions

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right
when such movement requires driving off the paved portion of the highway.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency).

'overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right' is the act drv.interaction.overtake_pass_on_right(subject, b), 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b on b's right'; b is of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

'driving off the paved portion of the highway': at some observation of the act the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') an st.shoulder whose paved attribute is unset ('the part of the highway beside the roadway ...; paved attribute'), or an st.road_edge whose paved attribute, 'for the surface beyond it', is unset, so that part of the body is at or beyond the edge of the pavement. 'requires' is read through the movement as made (reading). 'highway' keeps its extent: the paved portion is any paved part of it, so a paved shoulder or sidewalk is not 'off' it.

applicability: The subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, overtakes and passes on its right another road user b of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: drv.interaction.overtake_pass_on_right(subject, b) with p.overtake_window and p.overtake_same_direction_cos is recognized at the judged observation; b is quantified there, not a binder.
obligation: At no observation of the act, from its beginning (the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with aligned headings) to its recognition, does the subject's footprint overlap (rel.occupies) an st.shoulder whose paved attribute is unset or an st.road_edge whose paved attribute, for the surface beyond it, is unset; where it does at some such observation, the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes b on b's right with its footprint overlapping an st.shoulder whose paved attribute is unset during the side-by-side phase.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes b on b's right in the adjacent lane, its footprint overlapping no unpaved shoulder and no road edge with an unpaved surface beyond.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives along an unpaved shoulder with no road user ahead of it: no pass is recognized.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes b on its right; rel.occupies is not observed, so whether it overlapped an unpaved shoulder is unknown.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3
scenarios.narrative: The subject's footprint overlaps an unpaved shoulder during the middle part of the pass only, the rest of the act on the roadway.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject's footprint overlapped an unpaved shoulder only before the act began; it returned to the roadway, and then passed b on its right on the pavement.

under_way.words: overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right
under_way.justification: An observation inside the act lies after its beginning, the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, rel.same_direction), and at or before its recognition, while the subject's velocity (kin.velocity), exceeding b's along its heading, carries it up to and past b; an unpaved shoulder occupied before that observation is outside the act. These relations read the two road users' relative motion, never a place.

param_proposals.source: overtaking-manoeuvre durations in naturalistic driving studies

segmentation.text: A vehicle
must not be driven to the left side of the center of a two-lane, two-directional highway and overtaking and passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction,
unless such left side is clearly visible
and is free of oncoming traffic

for a sufficient distance ahead to permit such overtaking and passing to be completely made without interfering with the safe operation of any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction or any vehicle overtaken.

elements.justification: 'A vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'), claimed whole.

'center' (DEF-NRS-484A-040) is 'a continuous or broken line marked upon the surface of a highway ... to indicate each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions, and, if a line is not marked, it is an imaginary line in the highway equally distant from the edges or curbs': st.centre_line, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway', lying (st.on_way) on the st.highway the subject occupies (rel.occupies). 'to the left side of the center' is prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c), 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', being negative: the centre line lies to the right of the subject's reference point. 'two-directional highway' (DEF-NRS-484B-073) is 'an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions': the highway carries an st.centre_line, which divides 'the two directions of a two-way roadway', one roadway, so the way is undivided. 'two-lane': every st.lane lying on that highway (st.on_way) has an st.lane_adjacency 'count of the lanes in that direction' of a single lane, so the two directions carry the stated two lanes; the lane contract's exclusion ('lane ordinal equals roadway half only on a two-lane road') is met, the road being two-lane. 'overtaking and passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction' is the act drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b): 'a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; b is of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'driven' is read through controlled motion (agency).

'such left side is clearly visible': st.sight_distance at the subject's point, 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other ... whether or not any road user is there'; what a driver could see is read through that place's sight distance (observable_reading, perception), not rel.visible, since no actual road user need be there. Its extent is bounded by the standard of s7.

'oncoming traffic': road users of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic whose heading is opposed and closing to the subject's (rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing'); 'free of' them for the distance of s7 is read on their rel.centre_distance to the subject, which is not used as a clearance between bodies but as the distance along the road ahead.

operationalizations.standard: for a sufficient distance ahead to permit such overtaking and passing to be completely made without interfering with the safe operation of any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction or any vehicle overtaken
operationalizations.convention: Passing sight distance: the MUTCD minimum passing sight distance by prevailing speed (Table 3B-1), expressed as the time the subject's speed takes to cover it (p.passing_sight_time), so the required distance moves with the subject's speed; both the sight distance at the subject's point and the centre distance to every oncoming road user of traffic must reach it. Interference with the safe operation of an oncoming vehicle or the vehicle overtaken: the traffic-conflict technique, a contact or a closest approach under constant velocities within p.conflict_horizon closer than p.conflict_centre_clearance.

applicability: The subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, overtakes and passes another road user b of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b) with p.overtake_window and p.overtake_same_direction_cos is recognized at the judged observation. b is quantified there, not a binder.
obligation: At every observation of the act (from its beginning, the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead with aligned headings, to its recognition) at which the subject occupies a highway h on which an st.centre_line c lies (st.on_way) and every lane lying on h has a single lane in its direction (st.lane_adjacency count) — the two-lane, two-directional highway — and prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c) is negative for a centre line c lying on h (the subject on the left side of the center), all of the following hold; otherwise the duty is violated: st.sight_distance at the subject's point is at least the subject's kin.speed times p.passing_sight_time; every road user u of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic with rel.oncoming(subject, u) under p.oncoming_heading_cos is at a rel.centre_distance of at least that same distance; and neither b nor any road user u of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle oncoming to the subject is in rel.contact with the subject, or has prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u) over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'driven to the left side of the center' is read as the subject's reference point lying beyond the centre line to its left; a body that only straddles the line with its reference point on the right is not read.
'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.
'clearly visible' is read through the sight distance of the subject's place, what could be seen from it, not through any driver's perception.
The exception is read at the observations of the act at which the subject is on the left side of the center: visibility and freedom from oncoming traffic are required while the left side is used.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a highway with a centre line and one lane in each direction, the subject moves left of the centre line to pass b; a road user u of traffic is oncoming in that lane at a centre distance below the subject's speed times p.passing_sight_time, and its closest approach within p.conflict_horizon falls below p.conflict_centre_clearance; the pass is recognized.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same pass with st.sight_distance at the subject's point far above its speed times p.passing_sight_time at every observation of the act and no oncoming road user in the scene; the subject keeps clear of b.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject follows b on the two-lane highway without passing it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The pass of permit with st.sight_distance not observed on the source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes b on a highway with two lanes in each direction, using the other lane of its own direction, with an oncoming vehicle near on the far side of the centre line: the subject is never left of the centre of a two-lane highway.

scenarios.name: occasion_s5
scenarios.narrative: While the subject is left of the centre line, st.sight_distance at its point is above the subject's speed times p.passing_sight_time for the first part of the act and falls below it approaching a crest; no oncoming traffic.

scenarios.name: occasion_s5_outside
scenarios.narrative: st.sight_distance was below the bound before the act began and is above it at every observation of the act; no oncoming traffic.

scenarios.name: occasion_s6
scenarios.narrative: Sight distance is ample; an oncoming road user of traffic comes within the required distance during the second half of the act while the subject is still left of the centre line.

scenarios.name: occasion_s6_outside
scenarios.narrative: An oncoming road user passed the subject before the act began; during the act no oncoming road user is within the required distance.

under_way.words: overtaking and passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction
under_way.justification: An observation inside the act lies after its beginning, the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, rel.same_direction), and at or before its recognition, while the subject's velocity (kin.velocity), exceeding b's along its heading, carries it up to and past b. These relations read the two road users' relative motion, never a place.

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of an overtaking manoeuvre on an urban street, from having the overtaken vehicle ahead to having it behind
param_proposals.source: overtaking-manoeuvre durations in naturalistic driving studies

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as travelling in the same direction while one moves out to pass the other
param_proposals.source: lane-change heading angles in naturalistic driving data

param_proposals.name: p.passing_sight_time
param_proposals.convention: the MUTCD minimum passing sight distance (Table 3B-1, the warrant for a no-passing zone) divided by the prevailing speed it is tabulated for: about eleven seconds of travel across 25 to 70 mph; the sight distance or the clear distance a pass needs is the subject's speed times this time
param_proposals.source: MUTCD 2009 Section 3B.02, Table 3B-1

param_proposals.name: p.oncoming_heading_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as proceeding in opposite directions
param_proposals.source: heading geometry of two-way traffic

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique; FHWA Surrogate Safety Assessment Model

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO passenger-car design-vehicle dimensions

segmentation.text: A vehicle
must not be driven to the left side of the highway at any time:
When approaching the crest of a grade
or upon a curve in the highway
where the driver’s view is obstructed
within such distance as to create a hazard in the event another vehicle might approach from the opposite direction.
Subsection 2 does not apply upon a one-way highway.

elements.justification: 'A vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole.

'the left side of the highway' is the side beyond its center (DEF-NRS-484A-040: 'to indicate each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions, and, if a line is not marked, it is an imaginary line in the highway equally distant from the edges'): an st.centre_line c, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions', lying (st.on_way) on the st.highway the subject occupies (rel.occupies), with prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c) ('signed lateral offset (m, left positive)') negative: c lies to the right of the subject's reference point. 'at any time' places the duty at every observation. 'driven' is read through controlled motion (agency).

'the crest of a grade' is st.crest, 'the place on a roadway's longitudinal profile where the slope changes from rising to falling in the direction of travel ... so the ground distance from a road user to it is read through st.region_geometry'; not st.grade, whose contract says it is 'Not a stand-in for: the place of a crest'. 'approaching' is the subject's velocity (kin.velocity) pointing toward the crest's reference point from its position (kin.position): the dot product of the velocity with the vector from the position to that point is positive; the crest is anchored to the subject by its ground distance (st.region_geometry), bounded in s6.

'upon a curve in the highway': the subject occupies the st.highway (rel.occupies) and st.curvature, 'horizontal curvature of the roadway at a point, as a magnitude', at its point stands clear of zero by the source's resolution (p.curvature_resolution): a curve named without a size is its presence. Not kin.yaw_rate, which is 'Not a stand-in for: road curvature'.

'the driver's view is obstructed': st.sight_distance at the subject's point, 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other ... whether or not any road user is there', short of the distance of s6. What the driver could see is read through the sight distance of the place (observable_reading, perception), not rel.visible, since the other vehicle is hypothetical.
'upon a one-way highway': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) an st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'; there subsection 2 does not apply.

operationalizations.standard: within such distance as to create a hazard in the event another vehicle might approach from the opposite direction
operationalizations.convention: Passing sight distance: the MUTCD minimum passing sight distance by prevailing speed (Table 3B-1), the warrant for a no-passing zone at a crest or curve, expressed as the time the subject's speed takes to cover it. The hazard distance is the subject's kin.speed times p.passing_sight_time; the view is obstructed within it where st.sight_distance at the subject's point is below it, and a crest is approached within it where its ground distance (st.region_geometry) is at most it. The bound moves with the subject's speed.

applicability: At an observation at which the subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, occupies no st.one_way_roadway, st.sight_distance at its point is below the hazard distance (its kin.speed times p.passing_sight_time), and either (crest) for some st.crest k the subject's kin.velocity points toward k's reference point and the ground distance from the subject's body to k (st.region_geometry) is at most the hazard distance, or (curve) the subject occupies a highway and st.curvature at its point exceeds p.curvature_resolution.
obligation: The subject is not on the left side of the highway: for every st.centre_line c lying (st.on_way) on a highway the subject occupies, prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c) is not negative. Where it is negative for some such c, the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: 'driven to the left side of the highway' is read as the subject's reference point lying beyond the centre line to its left.
'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.
'the driver's view' is read through the sight distance of the subject's place, what could be seen from it, not through any driver's perception.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject moves toward an st.crest whose ground distance is below its speed times p.passing_sight_time; st.sight_distance at its point is below that distance; its reference point lies left of the centre line of the highway it occupies.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same approach to the crest with the subject right of the centre line (prim.region_lateral_offset to the line positive).

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: On a straight, level two-way highway (curvature at resolution, no crest ahead, sight distance far above the bound), the subject drives left of the centre line.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject is left of the centre line approaching a crest; st.sight_distance is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: On a curve (st.curvature above p.curvature_resolution) with st.sight_distance below the subject's speed times p.passing_sight_time and no crest, the subject is left of the centre line.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject approaches a crest with short sight distance on an st.one_way_roadway, left of the roadway's geometric centre.

param_proposals.name: p.passing_sight_time
param_proposals.convention: the MUTCD minimum passing sight distance (Table 3B-1, the warrant for a no-passing zone) divided by the prevailing speed it is tabulated for: about eleven seconds of travel across 25 to 70 mph; the sight distance or the clear distance a pass needs is the subject's speed times this time
param_proposals.source: MUTCD 2009 Section 3B.02, Table 3B-1

param_proposals.name: p.curvature_resolution
param_proposals.convention: the horizontal curvature at or below which a mapped roadway reads as straight: the curvature resolution of map centrelines (a radius of about two kilometres)
param_proposals.source: map centreline curvature resolution of the acquisition source

segmentation.text: A vehicle
must not be driven to the left side of the highway at any time:
When approaching within 100 feet or traversing any intersection or railroad grade crossing.
Subsection 2 does not apply upon a one-way highway.

elements.justification: 'A vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole.

'the left side of the highway' is the side beyond its center (DEF-NRS-484A-040: 'to indicate each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions, and, if a line is not marked, it is an imaginary line in the highway equally distant from the edges'): an st.centre_line c, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions', lying (st.on_way) on the st.highway the subject occupies (rel.occupies), with prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c) ('signed lateral offset (m, left positive)') negative. 'at any time' places the duty at every observation. 'driven' is read through controlled motion (agency).

'intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105) is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet', which excludes an alley junction as the definition's (3) does; 'railroad grade crossing' is st.railway_crossing, 'level crossing of a railway with the roadway' — a railroad (DEF-NRS-484A-200) is a carrier 'operated upon stationary rails' 'other than streetcars', and a streetcar line running in the street is no level crossing of a railway with the roadway. 'approaching within 100 feet': the ground distance from the subject's body to the region (st.region_geometry) is at most the stated 100 feet and the subject's velocity (kin.velocity) points toward the region's reference point from its position (kin.position). 'traversing': the subject's footprint overlaps the region (rel.occupies).
'upon a one-way highway': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) an st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'; there subsection 2 does not apply.

applicability: At an observation at which the subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, occupies no st.one_way_roadway and, for some region x of kind st.intersection or st.railway_crossing, either the subject's footprint overlaps x (rel.occupies), or the ground distance from its body to x (st.region_geometry) is at most the stated 100 feet and the dot product of its kin.velocity with the vector from its kin.position to x's reference point is positive.
obligation: The subject is not on the left side of the highway: for every st.centre_line c lying (st.on_way) on a highway the subject occupies, prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c) is not negative. Where it is negative for some such c, the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: 'driven to the left side of the highway' is read as the subject's reference point lying beyond the centre line to its left.
'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject moves toward an st.intersection whose ground distance from its body is below the stated 100 feet, with its reference point left of the centre line of the highway it occupies.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same approach with the subject right of the centre line.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is left of the centre line far from any intersection or railway crossing.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject moves toward an intersection with st.region_geometry not observed: its distance to the intersection and its offset from the centre line are unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject's footprint overlaps an st.railway_crossing while its reference point is left of the centre line.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject approaches an intersection within the stated distance on an st.one_way_roadway.

segmentation.text: A vehicle
must not be driven to the left side of the highway at any time:
When the view is obstructed
upon approaching within 100 feet of any bridge, viaduct or tunnel.
Subsection 2 does not apply upon a one-way highway.

elements.justification: 'A vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole.

'the left side of the highway' is the side beyond its center (DEF-NRS-484A-040: 'to indicate each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions, and, if a line is not marked, it is an imaginary line in the highway equally distant from the edges'): an st.centre_line c, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions', lying (st.on_way) on the st.highway the subject occupies (rel.occupies), with prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c) ('signed lateral offset (m, left positive)') negative. 'at any time' places the duty at every observation. 'driven' is read through controlled motion (agency).

'any bridge, viaduct or tunnel' is st.elevated_structure, 'bridge, viaduct or tunnel carrying the roadway'. 'approaching within 100 feet': the ground distance from the subject's body to the structure (st.region_geometry) is at most the stated 100 feet and the subject's velocity (kin.velocity) points toward the structure's reference point from its position (kin.position).
'upon a one-way highway': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) an st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'; there subsection 2 does not apply.

operationalizations.convention: Passing sight distance: the MUTCD minimum passing sight distance by prevailing speed (Table 3B-1), the warrant for a no-passing zone where the view is restricted, expressed as the time the subject's speed takes to cover it. The view is obstructed where st.sight_distance at the subject's point, 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other', is below the subject's kin.speed times p.passing_sight_time; the bound moves with the subject's speed.

applicability: At an observation at which the subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, occupies no st.one_way_roadway, st.sight_distance at its point is below its kin.speed times p.passing_sight_time, and for some st.elevated_structure x the ground distance from its body to x (st.region_geometry) is at most the stated 100 feet and the dot product of its kin.velocity with the vector from its kin.position to x's reference point is positive.
obligation: The subject is not on the left side of the highway: for every st.centre_line c lying (st.on_way) on a highway the subject occupies, prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c) is not negative. Where it is negative for some such c, the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: 'driven to the left side of the highway' is read as the subject's reference point lying beyond the centre line to its left.
'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.
'the view' is read through the sight distance of the subject's place, what could be seen from it, not through any driver's perception.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject moves toward an st.elevated_structure within the stated 100 feet, st.sight_distance at its point below its speed times p.passing_sight_time, its reference point left of the centre line.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same approach with the subject right of the centre line.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject approaches a bridge within the stated distance with st.sight_distance far above the bound, left of the centre line.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject approaches a bridge within the stated distance left of the centre line; st.sight_distance is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The same approach with short sight distance on an st.one_way_roadway.

param_proposals.name: p.passing_sight_time
param_proposals.convention: the MUTCD minimum passing sight distance (Table 3B-1, the warrant for a no-passing zone) divided by the prevailing speed it is tabulated for: about eleven seconds of travel across 25 to 70 mph; the sight distance or the clear distance a pass needs is the subject's speed times this time
param_proposals.source: MUTCD 2009 Section 3B.02, Table 3B-1

segmentation.text: A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course, shall be given continuously
during not less than the last 100 feet traveled
in a business or residential district
and not less than the last 300 feet traveled
in any other area
prior to changing the course
of a vehicle.
This rule shall be observed, regardless of the weather.

elements.justification: 'A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn ... from a direct course' is the signal itself, not a declared intention: sig.turn_indicator, 'the turn indicator state in {off, left, right}', to the side of the course change, or sig.hand_signal, 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning in {..., left, right, ...}', to that side; the indicator's exclusion (not the turn or lane change itself) does not apply, the words naming the signal. 'given continuously' is the signal holding at every observation of the window the next spans state. 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

'during not less than the last 100 feet traveled' is a .path window of the stated 100 feet of the subject's path behind the course change; the window reads kin.path_length, 'distance travelled along the body's path since the start of the trace'.
'not less than the last 300 feet traveled': a .path window of the stated 300 feet of the subject's path (kin.path_length) behind the course change.

'changing the course' is the onset of the subject's turn from a direct course: the observation at which, for an st.lane the subject occupies (rel.occupies), drv.lane.heading_left_of_carrier ('Road user a, moving, points to the left of the designated direction of travel of carrier region r by more than a tolerance') or drv.lane.heading_right_of_carrier rises; the side of the departure is the side the signal must show. A turn, a lane change and a pull-out each begin so; following the lane's own direction is keeping the course.
'of a vehicle': the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole: the subject is the vehicle whose course changes.

residues.why: The words exclude the weather as a ground for any other duty; the duty is the same whatever the weather, so they add no restriction.

applicability: The subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, changes course at the judged observation: for some st.lane l the subject occupies (rel.occupies), drv.lane.heading_left_of_carrier(subject, l) or drv.lane.heading_right_of_carrier(subject, l), with p.course_departure_sin_tol and p.halt_speed_tolerance, holds here and did not at the previous observation (rises). The trigger is read only where the subject occupies some lane (definedWhen): where it occupies none, the course change is unknown.
obligation: At that observation, for the side of the departure (left for heading_left_of_carrier, right for heading_right_of_carrier), the subject has shown sig.turn_indicator to that side or sig.hand_signal of meaning that side at every observation of the .path window of the subject's path behind it (holdsFor .path). The window is the stated 100 feet where asm.business_or_residence_district holds at that observation and the stated 300 feet where it does not (Term.cond); it is unknown where the assumption is undeclared or the window reaches before the recording. Otherwise the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: The side of the signal is the side the heading departs to; a departure that later reverses is judged at its own onset.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: asm.business_or_residence_district false; the subject moves in its lane with sig.turn_indicator off and sig.hand_signal no_signal, then its heading turns left of the lane's direction beyond p.course_departure_sin_tol (a lane change to the left).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: asm.business_or_residence_district false; the subject shows sig.turn_indicator left at every observation over the last stated 300 feet of its path before its heading departs to the left of its lane.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject keeps its heading along its lane's designated direction throughout; no course change begins.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject's heading departs to the right of its lane; neither sig.turn_indicator nor sig.hand_signal is observed on the source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: asm.business_or_residence_district true; the subject shows sig.turn_indicator right over a stretch of its path longer than the stated 100 feet but shorter than the stated 300 feet before its heading departs to the right of its lane.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1 with asm.business_or_residence_district false: the indicator was not shown over the last stated 300 feet.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: asm.business_or_residence_district false; the subject shows sig.turn_indicator right over the last stated 300 feet and its heading departs to the left of its lane: the signal shows the wrong side.

param_proposals.name: p.course_departure_sin_tol
param_proposals.convention: sine of the largest angle (about two degrees) between a moving vehicle's heading and its lane's designated direction at which it counts as keeping its course: lane-keeping heading wander plus the source's heading noise, below the few degrees of heading a lane change takes
param_proposals.source: lane-keeping and lane-change heading-angle measurements in naturalistic driving data

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition source
